card.name: Punctuation before self-help explanations
card.fires_on: Colons, commas and linking words that come right before an explanation or advice in general-audience health, habit and learning articles. It marks the spot where a new point or definition is about to start.

modes.label: Colon before a point
modes.description: A colon that introduces a statement or definition in a self-improvement or fitness article.
modes.example: We won’t sugarcoat it for you<<:>> forming good habits can be tough.

modes.label: Comma after an opener
modes.description: A comma after a short opening phrase such as "In simple terms" or "Remember".
modes.example: In simple terms<<,>> metabolism refers to the rate at which we

modes.label: Linking word before a topic
modes.description: A small word such as "of" or "like" just before the topic noun is named.
modes.example: No one can emphasize enough the importance<< of>> brain development in early childhood education.

card.writes: It slightly favors nouns like trial, therapy, compartment and layer, so a topic or category noun tends to come next.
card.plain: It fires at the small pause marks in plain-language articles just before the writer states the main point.
